office.subject: reception
office.rationale: Visitors should meet a person or a desk as soon as they come in, so the reception sits at or within sight of the entry lobby rather than deeper in the plan.
exceptions: Buildings with a ground-floor shared lobby and a tenant reception on an upper floor, where the reception is next to the lift lobby instead
Fully self-service or badge-only workplaces

office.subject: main_entry
office.rationale: The entry opens onto a lobby that acts as a buffer, so outside weather, noise and strangers do not step straight into work areas.
exceptions: Small tenant suites where the front door opens directly onto the reception

office.subject: open_office
office.rationale: Work areas should be entered from shared circulation so that any room can be reached without passing through another team's space.
exceptions: Open plans where circulation is a zone inside the room rather than a separate corridor space
Small suites with a single open room

office.subject: meeting_room
office.condition: meeting room is intended for external visitors
office.rationale: Rooms used for outside guests are best close to the front, so visitors are not escorted through the working floor.
exceptions: Internal team meeting rooms are better close to the teams they serve
Security-sensitive tenants may deliberately keep visitors in a separate suite

office.subject: reception
office.condition: route from entry to visitor meeting rooms
office.rationale: The path a visitor takes from reception to a meeting room should not cut through desks, which protects privacy and focus.
exceptions: Showcase workplaces that intentionally display the work floor to guests

office.subject: meeting_room
office.rationale: People attend meetings from many teams, so meeting rooms are opened from shared circulation, not from inside a team's desks.
exceptions: Team-owned huddle rooms attached to a single department
Executive suites with private meeting rooms

office.subject: focus_room
office.rationale: Quiet rooms are placed away from noisy, high-traffic places such as the kitchen or break area so that they actually stay quiet.
exceptions: Small floors where distance is not achievable, mitigated by acoustic construction
Phone booths intentionally placed at the heart of the open plan for convenience

office.subject: restroom
office.rationale: Plumbing is cheapest stacked and shared with the vertical core, so restrooms are grouped beside the lifts and stairs and over each other on every floor.
exceptions: Renovations that reuse existing risers elsewhere
Very large floor plates needing more than one restroom group

office.subject: restroom
office.rationale: Restroom doors open onto circulation or a vestibule, never straight out of a meeting or work room, for privacy and hygiene.
exceptions: Private en-suite restrooms for an executive office
Accessible single-user restrooms attached to a suite

office.subject: open_office
office.condition: a restroom within a reasonable walk of every workstation
office.rationale: Occupants should not need to leave their floor or walk the full length of the building to reach a restroom, which a path-length check on the graph can test.
exceptions: The exact threshold is contested and varies by jurisdiction and employer policy
Multi-floor tenants sometimes concentrate facilities on one floor

office.subject: pantry
office.rationale: A break area close to the desks gets used and keeps people on the floor, though it should be separated acoustically from quiet zones.
exceptions: Central amenity floors that serve a whole building
Conflicts with the rule that focus rooms stay away from noise

office.subject: print_room
office.rationale: Shared printing and supplies are sited centrally on the circulation so that they serve many desks, with a door or wall to hold back noise and fumes.
exceptions: Increasingly paperless offices drop the room entirely
Large print equipment may be exiled to a service area

office.subject: it_room
office.rationale: Network and server closets are entered from controlled circulation and not through an occupied room, and they should be stacked vertically so cabling runs are short.
exceptions: Small offices where the cabinet sits in a storage room
Cloud-first tenants with only a minimal comms cabinet

office.subject: it_room
office.rationale: Equipment rooms should not sit directly under or beside wet rooms and plumbing risers, which reduces the chance of leak damage.
exceptions: Where there is no alternative on a tight floor, a drip tray and waterproofing may be used

office.subject: storage
office.rationale: Storage, supply and janitorial rooms are served from back-of-house circulation, keeping them off the visitor path and out of prime daylight zones.
exceptions: Team storage built into the open office
Janitor closets that are required to be near wet cores

clinic.subject: main_entry
clinic.rationale: Patients arrive into a waiting area with a clear view of the reception, so the first decision after the door is obvious.
exceptions: Clinics that use a separate lobby and then a department waiting room

clinic.subject: reception
clinic.rationale: Front desk staff need to see and greet patients, and to see who is waiting, so reception overlooks or opens into the waiting area.
exceptions: Kiosk-based check-in with a remote front desk
Cluster designs with a separate waiting zone per pod

clinic.subject: waiting_room
clinic.rationale: Patients are called from waiting into a clinical corridor leading to exam rooms; they do not walk through staff areas.
exceptions: Small clinics where waiting opens straight into a single exam room

clinic.subject: exam_room
clinic.rationale: Every exam room opens to a corridor so that patients and clinicians reach it without crossing another exam room.
exceptions: Paired exam rooms sharing a consult or procedure room
Dental or ophthalmic suites with open bays

clinic.subject: exam_room
clinic.rationale: Conversations in exam rooms should not be audible in the waiting area, and door swings should not open onto a view of the patient; a buffer corridor or acoustic wall is used.
exceptions: Very small clinics where they share a wall and rely on sound-rated construction

clinic.subject: staff_room
clinic.rationale: Staff break, charting and work areas are not entered from the public waiting area, so staff can rest and talk without patients overhearing.
exceptions: A door from reception to a back office is often needed, which is acceptable if it is controlled

clinic.subject: nurse_station
clinic.rationale: A team base in the middle of the exam rooms keeps clinicians within a short walk of every room and gives line of sight to the corridor.
exceptions: Layouts with decentralised alcoves at each pod
Very small practices with no distinct nurse station

clinic.subject: clean_supply
clinic.rationale: Clean supplies are kept in a room that clinical staff can reach quickly but patients and soiled material cannot pass through.
exceptions: Wall-mounted stock in each exam room replaces a central supply room
Off-site sterile processing

clinic.subject: soiled_utility
clinic.rationale: Soiled items and waste are kept in a different room from clean stock and should not be carried across the clean room's door.
exceptions: Very small clinics may use one room with a physical and procedural separation, which is contested and may not be allowed locally

clinic.subject: soiled_utility
clinic.rationale: Waste and soiled items move through staff or service corridors, not through patient-facing space.
exceptions: Small clinics where the only route to the waste room passes a shared corridor

clinic.subject: patient_restroom
clinic.rationale: Patients often need a restroom before or after a visit, and sample collection needs a restroom reachable by the patient and the lab or staff.
exceptions: A second restroom is often placed within the exam zone for patients mid-visit

clinic.subject: patient_restroom
clinic.condition: clinic collects urine or other samples
clinic.rationale: A pass-through hatch from the restroom to the collection space lets patients leave a sample without handling or carrying it.
exceptions: Clinics that do not collect samples
Some designs prefer patients carry samples to a desk, which is debated for privacy

clinic.subject: procedure_room
clinic.condition: clinic does minor procedures or sedation
clinic.rationale: Patients who have had a procedure move short distances to a supervised recovery area under staff view.
exceptions: No procedure services
Recovery in the same room for simple procedures

clinic.subject: patient_corridor
clinic.condition: wide enough for wheelchair and a person passing, and turning in exam rooms
clinic.rationale: Clinical corridors and exam rooms are sized for wheelchairs, gurneys and companions; a graph carries the widths as attributes.
exceptions: The exact widths differ by jurisdiction; treat any value in the pack as to be verified against local requirements

hospital.subject: public_circulation
hospital.rationale: Visitors, staff and supplies and waste each need their own route for infection control, privacy and efficient logistics; in the graph the public and service networks should meet only at controlled points.
exceptions: Lifts are often shared with timed or controlled use
Smaller hospitals frequently combine staff and service routes

hospital.subject: emergency_department
hospital.rationale: Emergency patients arrive by ambulance and on foot at a dedicated, clearly visible entrance, separate from the main lobby, so urgent cases do not queue with outpatients.
exceptions: Very small hospitals may combine the main and emergency entrances after hours

hospital.subject: ambulance_bay
hospital.rationale: The most critical patients should travel the shortest path from the ambulance to resuscitation, without crossing the waiting area.
exceptions: Some layouts route via a triage bay first
Helicopter arrivals arrive via a lift or a roof route

hospital.subject: main_entry
hospital.rationale: Visitors and outpatients arrive in one lobby with information and registration, from which the public circulation fans out to departments and lifts.
exceptions: Campuses with several entrances each serving a clinic block

hospital.subject: nurse_station
hospital.rationale: Nurse stations sit within a short walk and ideally line of sight of the patient rooms they serve, which shortens response times.
exceptions: Decentralised nursing with small alcoves at every few rooms is increasingly common and arguably better
Evidence on optimal layout is mixed

hospital.subject: patient_room
hospital.rationale: Inpatient rooms are reached via the ward and its staff station, not straight from public corridors, to control visitors and protect privacy.
exceptions: Public corridors in some designs are the ward's visitor corridor and are controlled by a door at the unit entrance

hospital.subject: clean_utility
hospital.rationale: Clean stock and soiled or waste material are in separate rooms with separate routes, to avoid cross-contamination.
exceptions: Pass-through rooms may link the two by design, but the passage is one-way

hospital.subject: sterile_processing
hospital.condition: dirty instruments out, sterile instruments in, via separate routes
hospital.rationale: Instruments move from theatre to decontamination, then to clean packing and sterile storage, and back to the theatre on a one-way path; ideally a dedicated lift or pass-through serves the two.
exceptions: Off-site or shared central sterile processing
Small day-surgery units may use combined spaces

hospital.subject: operating_theatre
hospital.rationale: The surgical suite is a restricted zone entered through a changing and scrub transition, which keeps street clothes and visitors out.
exceptions: Emergency access for patients arriving from the emergency department
Hybrid theatres that have extra staff entrances

hospital.subject: intensive_care
hospital.rationale: Critical patients move between ICU, theatres, imaging and the emergency department, so these are grouped or stacked with a direct lift where possible.
exceptions: A hospital cannot place all departments adjacent to each other; priorities depend on case mix
Vertical adjacency by lift often replaces horizontal adjacency

hospital.subject: imaging
hospital.rationale: The emergency department is a heavy user of CT and X-ray, so imaging close by shortens patient transport in urgent cases.
exceptions: Some hospitals keep a satellite scanner in the ED and the main imaging dept elsewhere
Imaging is also needed by outpatients, which pulls it toward the public front

hospital.subject: isolation_room
hospital.rationale: Rooms for airborne infections are entered through a small lobby so pressure differences can be held and staff can put on protection.
exceptions: Protective-environment rooms use the same anteroom with the opposite pressure direction
Some jurisdictions allow a single room with no anteroom for droplet isolation

hospital.subject: loading_dock
hospital.rationale: Deliveries, linen, waste and food enter and leave at a dock outside public view and move on service routes to stores, kitchen and the soiled holding area.
exceptions: Pneumatic tubes or automated guided vehicles reduce reliance on corridors
Urban sites with a shared dock

hospital.subject: mortuary
hospital.rationale: The mortuary is reached by a discreet service route that avoids patient and visitor areas, with its own external access for funeral directors.
exceptions: Small hospitals may share the service lift but time its use

hospital.subject: pharmacy
hospital.rationale: Pharmacy stock including controlled drugs needs access control and a loading route from the dock, while the outpatient window may face the public side.
exceptions: An outpatient pharmacy has a public counter by definition
Robotic dispensing changes the layout

hospital.subject: outpatient_waiting
hospital.rationale: Outpatient clinics are visited by people who are mostly well enough to walk, so their waiting areas open straight off public circulation near the lobby, keeping clinic traffic out of the wards and the service routes.
exceptions: Specialty clinics inside an inpatient unit, such as dialysis or oncology day wards, may sit behind a unit door
Large campuses with a separate outpatient building replace the shared lobby with a building entrance

hospital.subject: exam_room
hospital.condition: clinic pod with a staff work area behind the rooms
hospital.rationale: A second door or a back route to the exam rooms lets clinicians move between rooms and the team work area without crossing the patient corridor, and lets patients be seen at the front while staff stay out of view.
exceptions: Many compact designs use a single corridor shared by patients and staff, which is cheaper and works for small pods
Evidence for the benefit of a dual-corridor pod is mixed and depends on throughput
An extra door in each room costs wall length and can weaken acoustic privacy

hospital.subject: exam_room
hospital.rationale: Exam room doors open onto a clinical corridor and not onto the waiting area, so a patient being examined or dressing cannot be seen or heard from the seats; the graph check is that no exam room is a direct neighbour of the waiting space.
exceptions: Single-room practices where the waiting area has no other route to the room
Fast-track or minor-injury bays that deliberately open from a shared treatment hall
A graph cannot show door swing or sightlines, so a human should still review the drawing

hospital.subject: clean_utility
hospital.condition: outpatient clinic pod with a central team base
hospital.rationale: Clinic staff restock exam rooms many times a day, so clean supplies sit beside the team base on the staff side, where stock can be reached quickly, while the soiled utility is placed on the same staff side but on a different route out.
exceptions: Wall cabinets or carts in each exam room can replace a central clean room
Clinics served by an automated supply system or a courier cart may place stores far from the team base
The soiled utility is placed on the clinic's staff side too, and how far apart the two rooms must be is contested

hospital.subject: patient_restroom
hospital.condition: clinic collects urine or other specimens
hospital.rationale: Patient restrooms are reachable from the waiting area without walking through the exam zone, and where specimens are taken a pass-through shelf to the lab or the nurse side avoids carrying samples through public space.
exceptions: Clinics that do not collect samples
Some designs hand samples over at a desk, which is debated for privacy
A second restroom inside the exam zone is often needed for patients mid-visit

datacenter.subject: data_hall
datacenter.rationale: The IT space is reached through a two-door vestibule that only lets one door open at a time and so prevents tailgating.
exceptions: Some operators use a single card and biometric door with a turnstile instead
Smaller edge sites

datacenter.subject: mantrap
datacenter.rationale: Access is layered from the site perimeter to the lobby, security desk, a controlled corridor and then the mantrap, so each layer is a separate check.
exceptions: Unmanned lights-out sites rely on remote access control

datacenter.subject: visitor_lobby
datacenter.rationale: Visitors and contractors stay in the front of the building and never get a direct door into the critical space.
exceptions: Customer-facing colocation sites with escorted tours that pass a viewing window

datacenter.subject: staging_room
datacenter.rationale: Equipment is unpacked and tested in a staging area close to the dock, so cardboard, dust and untested devices stay out of the data hall.
exceptions: Hyperscale sites receive pre-integrated racks straight from the dock into the hall

datacenter.subject: loading_dock
datacenter.rationale: A wide, step-free route links the dock, staging and halls so that heavy racks can be moved without crossing office or visitor space.
exceptions: Multi-storey designs with a goods lift instead of a corridor

datacenter.subject: electrical_room
datacenter.rationale: Switchgear, UPS and batteries sit in their own fire-rated rooms next to the halls and not inside them, which limits fire spread and keeps maintenance out of the IT white space.
exceptions: Modular or containerised designs put power inside the unit
Some small rooms put a UPS in the hall

datacenter.subject: electrical_room_a
datacenter.rationale: Two independent power paths serve each critical load, and their rooms, feeders and routes are in separate fire compartments so one event cannot take out both.
exceptions: Lower resilience tiers use only a single path with a spare
Some sites accept a shared wall with a high fire rating

datacenter.subject: mechanical_room_a
datacenter.rationale: Chilled water or air handling is split into independent halves with separate rooms and pipework, so a leak or failure in one does not stop all cooling.
exceptions: N+1 pooled designs share a ring main with isolation valves rather than two separate rooms
Resilience level varies, so the rule is a choice and not a universal

datacenter.subject: generator_yard
datacenter.rationale: Generators and fuel storage are outdoors or in separate enclosures away from the hall, for noise, exhaust, fire and vibration reasons, and connect by protected electrical routes.
exceptions: Indoor generator halls in dense urban sites
Rooftop plant

datacenter.subject: mechanical_room
datacenter.rationale: Air handling and cooling equipment sit close to the hall to shorten air or pipe runs and reduce loss, while remaining outside the IT space for maintenance.
exceptions: Rooftop or exterior chillers
In-row cooling inside the hall

datacenter.subject: data_hall
datacenter.rationale: Pipes, drains and wet plant are kept away from the IT space to limit leak risk; if there is a connecting door it is a rated door into a corridor, not a direct route.
exceptions: Many layouts do connect hall and cooling directly for air distribution
Liquid cooling puts water in the hall by design, which makes this rule contested

datacenter.subject: network_operations_center
datacenter.rationale: The monitoring room is in the secured area, often in view of the entry control, but outside the data hall to keep people from working among the racks.
exceptions: Remote or off-site NOC
Staff sitting in the front office with remote monitoring

datacenter.subject: data_hall
datacenter.rationale: Each hall is in its own fire compartment, so a fire in one hall does not spread to the next, and gas or pre-action suppression can be zoned.
exceptions: Small single-hall facilities
Required rating differs by jurisdiction and insurer

datacenter.subject: office
datacenter.rationale: Administration, break and meeting spaces sit outside the secure zone with their own entry and circulation, so ordinary staff do not need access to the white space.
exceptions: Technicians' work benches and burn-in rooms may be inside the secure zone

datacenter.subject: data_hall
datacenter.condition: room for racks, containment, overhead cable trays and air movement
datacenter.rationale: Halls need taller ceilings than ordinary rooms to carry containment, trays and airflow, so clear height is a graph attribute to check.
exceptions: The right number depends on the cooling approach and rack height; treat any given value as indicative and verify it

airport.subject: landside
airport.rationale: The public zone and the zone for screened passengers and staff are separate, joined only through controlled crossing points such as the security checkpoint.
exceptions: Transit passengers may stay airside throughout a connection
Some small airports have little formal separation

airport.subject: airside
airport.condition: for departing passengers starting on the landside
airport.rationale: A passenger starting on landside can only reach airside by passing screening, so screening is the single choke point in the graph for that path.
exceptions: Staff and crew use separate, controlled entries
Arrivals from international transfer have their own screening arrangements

airport.subject: check_in
airport.rationale: Check-in and bag drop are in the landside departures hall, ahead of security, so that a passenger deposits luggage before entering the screened area.
exceptions: Online check-in and off-airport check-in skip the desks
Some airports check in at the security line

airport.subject: departures_hall
airport.rationale: Departing passengers are dropped at a kerb that leads directly to check-in, so luggage-laden travellers have a short walk from road or rail.
exceptions: Rail or transit station entries rather than a road kerb
Multi-level designs where the departures kerb is on an upper deck

airport.subject: arrivals_route
airport.rationale: Arriving and departing passengers are kept on separate paths, often on different levels, so that arriving travellers cannot mix with screened passengers or pass items to them.
exceptions: Smaller single-level terminals use a shared concourse with time or door control
Domestic arrivals may be walkway-separated rather than level-separated

airport.subject: arrivals_gate_corridor
airport.rationale: International arrivals walk from the aircraft through border control to baggage reclaim and then customs, in that order, before reaching the public hall.
exceptions: Domestic arrivals skip border control and go straight to baggage reclaim
Order of reclaim and border control differs between airports

airport.subject: baggage_reclaim
airport.rationale: Reclaim belts sit past border control so passengers collect luggage once they have been admitted.
exceptions: Pre-clearance or preclearance setups
Domestic flows

airport.subject: baggage_makeup
airport.rationale: The sorting and make-up area is close to the apron so bags travel a short, enclosed route to aircraft, and it is a back-of-house space off any public route.
exceptions: Remote bag halls linked by long conveyors or tunnels
Off-airport baggage sorting

airport.subject: baggage_makeup
airport.rationale: Checked bags are screened in-line before they reach the make-up area, so nothing unscreened enters the airside bag flow.
exceptions: Screening may take place at the check-in desk or off-site
Oversize bags are screened by a separate process

airport.subject: check_in
airport.rationale: Bag drop is connected to screening by short conveyors; the more the two are separated, the longer and costlier the belts.
exceptions: Centralised screening hall serving several terminals
Off-airport check-in

airport.subject: gate
airport.rationale: Boarding gates open off a concourse that leads back to the security exit and the airside facilities.
exceptions: Bus gates that lead to a ground-level lounge and a bus
Remote stands reached by walking

airport.subject: gate
airport.rationale: A gate lounge connects to a boarding bridge or apron door so that boarding passengers do not cross other passenger flows.
exceptions: Walk-out gates without a bridge
Gates that flex between international and domestic use

airport.subject: retail
airport.condition: retail and food lie on the path between security and gates
airport.rationale: Shops and food outlets sit immediately after security and before the gates so passengers walk through them, which drives sales and gives a sense of waiting time.
exceptions: The walk-through model is contested for passenger comfort
Small airports put little retail in the path

airport.subject: international_pier
airport.rationale: International and domestic passengers are kept apart on the airside because of different border requirements, with swing gates that switch use only through a controlled door.
exceptions: Shared areas in countries without border control within a region
Flexible gates that need extra door control

airport.subject: staff_screening
airport.rationale: Workers pass through their own checkpoint and have their own circulation to airside, which keeps passenger queues free of staff traffic.
exceptions: Small airports share one checkpoint with a staff lane
